title: Mac Miller's 'The Divine Feminine' 10th Anniversary Edition Features 3 Unreleased Songs | Entertainment
text:
Mac Miller's estate announces The Divine Feminine 10th anniversary edition with three unreleased songs, including Butterflies, Grand, and Channel 13, out now.
Mac Miller's estate has announced a 10th-anniversary edition of his album The Divine Feminine, featuring three previously unreleased songs. The new tracks include Butterflies, released in September, while Grand and Channel 13 became available on streaming services for the first time on Friday.
The announcement was made by Mac Miller's estate and follows other posthumous releases from the late rapper. The 10th-anniversary edition aims to celebrate the original album's legacy with additional material for fans.
Unreleased Tracks and Production Details
The three unreleased songs are Butterflies, Grand, and Channel 13. Butterflies was released in September, while Grand and Channel 13 hit streaming services for the first time on Friday. Sam Balaban will be producing, directing, and editing the live special, with Bart Peters serving as the original live performance director. Contributions from E. Dan and Justin Boyd are also included.
The live special is part of the anniversary celebration, though specific air dates or platforms were not provided. The production team brings together experienced professionals to honor Mac Miller's work.
Cinderella Resurgence and Chart Success
Album standout Cinderella, featuring Ty Dolla $ign, experienced a massive resurgence this summer. A TikTok trend caused the eight-minute track exploring love and lust to explode in popularity. It reached a new peak at No. 25 on the Billboard Hot 100.
It is Mac Miller's second-highest charting single as a lead artist and is still surging. Cinderella also hit the top 10 of the latest Billboard Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart. The song's renewed success highlights its enduring appeal.
Background on The Divine Feminine and Mac Miller
The Divine Feminine was originally released in 2016 and marked a departure for Mac Miller, focusing on themes of love, relationships, and femininity. The album featured collaborations with artists like Ty Dolla $ign, Ariana Grande, and Anderson .Paak. It received critical acclaim and solidified Mac Miller's artistic growth.
Mac Miller, born Malcolm James McCormick, was a rapper, singer, and producer from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. He died in September 2018 at the age of 26. His estate has continued to release posthumous projects, including the album Circles in 2020. The 10th-anniversary edition of The Divine Feminine adds to his legacy.
The anniversary edition is now available, offering fans a chance to revisit the album with new material. The live special and unreleased tracks serve as a tribute to Mac Miller's impact on music.
